name: Facet
text:
Adopt a **system-wide dark theme by default** with a **one-click toggle to light mode**.

Dark themes reduce eye strain in low light and improve focus by minimizing glare, which aligns with our goal of clarity and liveliness. The toggle respects user preference without complicating the interface, accepting that some users may prefer light mode despite the default. This matches our competitors’ dark-themed dashboards while keeping the option flexible.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A system-wide dark theme by default locks out users with light sensitivity—this isn’t just a niche issue. A one-click toggle still fragments the experience—users switch mid-session, breaking flow and slowing them down. The real test is A/B testing with light sensitivity users and measuring task completion time; if the toggle adds friction, we need a dynamic system that adapts to ambient light instead.

name: Facet
text:
Adopt a **system-wide dark theme by default** with **no light mode toggle**.

Dark mode reduces eye strain and glare in low light, aligning with clarity and focus. Forcing consistency eliminates fragmentation—users won’t pause to switch modes mid-task. The trade-off is excluding users who prefer light mode, but we prioritize the majority’s comfort and the interface’s cohesion.

text: Pane: Forcing a single theme locks out users who need light mode for readability—this isn’t just preference, it’s accessibility. A better alternative is a system-wide default with a persistent, non-modal toggle that remembers user choice across sessions. name: Facet
text:
Adopt a **system-wide dark theme by default** with a **one-click toggle to light mode** and **no auto-switching**.

Dark mode reduces eye strain in low light and keeps focus sharp, which matches our clarity and liveliness goals. A single toggle avoids fragmentation—users choose once and stay in flow. The trade-off is accepting that light-sensitive users must manually switch, but this keeps the interface simple and consistent for everyone else.

name: Pane
text: Pane: The one-click toggle still forces users to preemptively pick a mode before they know how it feels—light sensitivity isn’t binary, and a wrong choice mid-task breaks rhythm. Better alternative: let the system learn from usage patterns (e.g., time-of-day, glare detection) and auto-adjust, with a manual override that remembers the user’s last override. Settle it with a 2-week A/B test tracking task completion time and user-reported strain in both groups.
